Faire partie de la communauté BIPOC* est: Being part of the BIPOC* community is one thing; being part of the 2SLGBTQ+** community, openly or not, is another. For many Montrealers, standing at the intersection of the two creates a unique life experience. In a modern Montréal where queer identity is proudly showcased, particularly during Pride events, a good part of this community nevertheless seems to be pushed aside, or even completely forgotten.
Si Montréal est souvent considérée comme: While Montréal is often seen as “a city where there's always something to do,” the reality is that the city's social life isn't necessarily adapted to everyone's reality.
Organisés par Project 10 dans le cadre d: Organized by Project 10 as part of the FULL CIRCLE project, the QTBIPOC TALKSPACES are open conversations for young people aged 18 to 25 in which different themes are explored. The goal of these gatherings is to open up dialogue among members of the QUEER-BIPOC community so they can share stories and experiences, but also tips and ideas to support one another.
<strong>Quand ?</strong> Le troisième je: When? The third Thursday of every month, from 6 p.m. to 8 p.m.
Sweet Like Honey organise des événements: Sweet Like Honey organizes events for people who relate to the lesbian and sapphic experience. Most of the time, these are music events or performances by local artists. Sweet Like Honey also showcases local BIPOC artists and talent in Montréal.
Le prochain événement est, par exemple,: The next event, for example, is a “Kookie Karaoke,” organized to let people from the queer BIPOC community express themselves through song. The event is free.
Les informations sur les événements sont: Event information is available on Sweet Like Honey's Instagram account: @sweetlikehoneymtl
Pour des événements lesbiens et <em>quee: For lesbian and queer events, ellelui organizes a host of nights with a varied program. Whether it's speed dating nights, open mics or visual art exhibitions, ellelui always puts this type of event front and centre.
Créé en 2019 dans le but de proposer des: Created in 2019 to offer activities that highlight people who do not identify with traditional gender configurations, Blush Party Montreal organizes events with queer artists (dancers, DJs, VJs, etc.) in order to promote the queer BIPOC community in the arts scene.
Les informations sur les événements sont: Event information is available on Blush Party's Instagram account: @blush.party
<strong>OÙ ALLER ?</strong><em> Quelques: WHERE TO GO? A few safe places for the queer BIPOC community
Consciente que les récits de personnes <: Aware that the stories of queer and BIPOC people don't fit a single mould, La Converse looked into the importance of Montréal venues considered safe for the people concerned.
On entend par « lieux » divers endroits,: By “venues,” we mean a variety of places, depending on their purpose, that are “BIPOC and queer-friendly,” among other things for their safety and for the openness they show toward the community through concrete actions.
Food-n-Ting désigne une série d’événemen: Food-n-Ting is a series of monthly events that set up food banks, along with skill-sharing, food, art and music. All events are free or very affordable, putting them within reach of marginalized populations. The goal of Food-n-Ting is to create a safer, judgment-free environment where Black, Indigenous and people of colour can gather, learn and eat together.
Le bar Notre-Dame-des-Quilles est situé: Bar Notre-Dame-des-Quilles is located on rue Beaubien. In addition to being “BIPOC and queer-friendly,” the place hosts many events throughout the year organized by and for the queer community in Montréal. The bar is offering, for example, a “BIPOC Pride market” on June 29.
Située dans le village, la librairie l’E: Located in the Village, the bookstore L'Euguélionne is a non-profit cooperative. It offers works of women's and feminist literature, as well as queer, lesbian, gay, bisexual, trans, intersex, asexual and agender, two-spirit, anti-racist and anti-colonial literature, among others. It is also a safe gathering place where many events are held, including book launches for LGBTQ+ authors and activities organized in collaboration with other BIPOC organizations.
La librairie indépendante Un livre à soi: The independent bookstore Un livre à soi, located near the Plateau-Mont-Royal, opened its doors in 2022. The shop regularly features queer BIPOC books and authors, and hosts many literary events where the queer BIPOC community is valued and safe.
AGIR (Action LGBTQIA+ avec les Immigrant: AGIR (Action LGBTQIA+ avec les ImmigrantEs et RéfugiéEs) is a non-profit organization based in Montréal that works with the migrant queer community. AGIR offers a wide range of services in four languages (French, English, Spanish and Arabic).
Entre soutien personnalisé et activités: From personalized support to group activities (closed or open), AGIR also offers all kinds of education and awareness programs. The training sessions and workshops are designed to raise awareness among the public and the people concerned about the rights of the queer community, specifically the migrant queer community.
AGIR accompagne les personnes <em>queer<: AGIR supports queer and BIPOC people as they adjust to life in Montréal, notably by providing direct assistance (legal or medical aid, for example). AGIR has also prepared a Guide à l'intention des prestataires de services qui interviennent auprès des personnes trans+ et non-binaires migrantes et réfugiées.
Helem Montréal est un organisme qui lutt: Helem Montréal is an organization that fights the homophobia faced by Montréal's Arabic-speaking community. Helem also sees itself as a staunch defender of the rights of LGBTQ+ people and works to promote everyone's inclusion in the face of prejudice.
Dans le but de créer un Montréal plus sé: With the aim of creating a safer Montréal for the queer Arabic-speaking community, Helem regularly organizes activities and events meant to create spaces for awareness.
The Lavender Collective est un collectif: The Lavender Collective is a collective formed by Black people advocating for the mental health needs of racialized people and marginalized communities. It offers a list of direct resources (available by phone or in person) to help the people concerned, depending on their circumstances.
Les personnes <em>queer</em> BIPOC viven: Queer BIPOC people face unique situations in Montréal, and The Lavender Collective is aware of this. It therefore offers emergency resources intended for them.
Pour le moment, les activités de The Lav: For the moment, The Lavender Collective's activities are suspended. Its resources are still available on the organization's website.
Jhalak Montréal est un organisme soutena: Jhalak Montréal is an organization supporting LGBTQ+ people from South Asian communities. It organizes events meant to raise awareness among Montrealers about the South Asian queer reality, including education and awareness workshops on important issues.
